lines: -\looseness=-1 SCB is structural: BR $1.66$--$4.97\times$ across nine models, MAX-SAT identical to count-only on 94.4\% of problems, vote diversity collapsed ($K_{\text{eff}} = 1.20$--$3.62$, $K{=}12$), and all 27 interventions at $\kappa \geq 0.40$ \citep{huang2024selfcorrect, stechly2025selfverification}. Cross-architecture NLI escapes when the verifier exceeds the generator ($p = 0.003$); diagnostics ($K_\text{eff}$, BR, $C_0$) predict failure (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).

+\looseness=-1 Three zero-cost diagnostics predict self-verification failure before deployment. $K_\text{eff} \leq 1.3$ signals that symbolic aggregation collapses to majority voting (Qwen2.5-14B FOLIO: $K_\text{eff} = 1.20$, $\Delta = -0.98$\,pp). SC $< 40\%$ means constraints amplify errors rather than correct them (Mistral-7B PW: $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp). $C_0 < 5\%$ indicates near-unanimous traces, rendering all aggregation moot. Only the intermediate regime (SC $\sim$50--60\%, $K_\text{eff} > 1.8$) offers marginal gain potential; practitioners should compute these metrics before investing in symbolic reasoning infrastructure.

+\looseness=-1 SCB extends to any method extracting structured representations from a model's own outputs---self-verification \citep{huang2024selfcorrect}, self-refinement \citep{madaan2023selfrefine}, and chain-of-verification \citep{dhuliawala2023chainofverification} all face the same distributional prior. Our debate control ($\kappa = 0.15$, $-18.6$\,pp) confirms that breaking within-model correlation sacrifices accuracy: independence and quality are at odds under same-model constraints. Any pipeline that asks a model to critique, verify, or formalize its own reasoning risks inheriting SCB.

+\looseness=-1 The cross-architecture escape (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}) identifies three necessary conditions for effective post-hoc verification: (i)~\emph{structural independence}---the verifier must not share architecture or training data with the generator; (ii)~\emph{positive capability gap}---the verifier's independence-adjusted contribution must exceed the generator's SC; (iii)~\emph{task-verifier alignment}---the verification paradigm must match the task structure. These explain why 27 same-model interventions fail ($\kappa \geq 0.40$) while a 406M encoder-only model succeeds ($+11.00$\,pp). Future systems should prioritize structural complementarity over raw capability; trained extractors capturing $>$12\% of the oracle ceiling ($+29.90$\,pp) represent the most promising direction (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).

+\looseness=-1 In summary, formal self-verification creates a \emph{symbolic mirage}: provably sound machinery that adds no information beyond majority voting. The path forward lies in structurally independent external verification, guided by the $K_\text{eff}$, BR, and $C_0$ diagnostics introduced here.

\looseness=-1 SCB extends to any method extracting structured representations from a model's own outputs---self-verification \citep{huang2024selfcorrect}, self-refinement \citep{madaan2023selfrefine}, and chain-of-verification \citep{dhuliawala2023chainofverification} all face the same distributional prior. Our debate control ($\kappa = 0.15$, $-18.6$\,pp) confirms that breaking within-model correlation sacrifices accuracy: independence and quality are at odds under same-model constraints. Any pipeline that asks a model to critique, verify, or formalize its own reasoning risks inheriting SCB.

input.old_string: \looseness=-1 The cross-architecture escape (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}) identifies three necessary conditions for effective post-hoc verification: (i)~\emph{structural independence}---the verifier must not share architecture or training data with the generator; (ii)~\emph{positive capability gap}---the verifier's independence-adjusted contribution must exceed the generator's SC; (iii)~\emph{task-verifier alignment}---the verification paradigm must match the task structure. These explain why 27 same-model interventions fail ($\kappa \geq 0.40$) while a 406M encoder-only model succeeds ($+11.00$\,pp). Future systems should prioritize structural complementarity over raw capability; trained extractors capturing $>$12\% of the oracle ceiling ($+29.90$\,pp) represent the most promising direction (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}).

\looseness=-1 In summary, formal self-verification creates a \emph{symbolic mirage}: provably sound machinery that adds no information beyond majority voting. The path forward lies in structurally independent external verification, guided by the $K_\text{eff}$, BR, and $C_0$ diagnostics introduced here.

lines: \looseness=-1 Three zero-cost diagnostics predict self-verification failure before deployment. $K_\text{eff} \leq 1.3$: symbolic aggregation collapses to majority voting ($\Delta = -0.98$\,pp). SC $< 40\%$: constraints amplify errors ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp). $C_0 < 5\%$: near-unanimous traces render aggregation moot. Only the intermediate regime (SC $\sim$50--60\%, $K_\text{eff} > 1.8$) offers marginal gain; practitioners should compute these before investing in symbolic reasoning.

-\looseness=-1 SCB extends to any method extracting structured representations from a model's own outputs---self-verification \citep{huang2024selfcorrect}, self-refinement \citep{madaan2023selfrefine}, and chain-of-verification \citep{dhuliawala2023chainofverification} all face the same distributional prior. Our debate control ($\kappa = 0.15$, $-18.6$\,pp) confirms that breaking within-model correlation sacrifices accuracy: independence and quality are at odds under same-model constraints. Any pipeline that asks a model to critique, verify, or formalize its own reasoning risks inheriting SCB.

+\looseness=-1 SCB extends to any method extracting structured representations from a model's own outputs---self-verification \citep{huang2024selfcorrect}, self-refinement \citep{madaan2023selfrefine}, and chain-of-verification \citep{dhuliawala2023chainofverification} all face the same distributional prior. Our debate control ($\kappa = 0.15$, $-18.6$\,pp) confirms that independence and quality are at odds under same-model constraints.

\looseness=-1 The cross-architecture escape (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}) identifies three necessary conditions: (i)~\emph{structural independence}---no shared architecture or training data; (ii)~\emph{positive capability gap}---the verifier's adjusted contribution exceeds the generator's SC; (iii)~\emph{task-verifier alignment}---the verification paradigm matches task structure. These explain why 27 same-model interventions fail ($\kappa \geq 0.40$) while a 406M encoder succeeds ($+11.00$\,pp). Trained extractors capturing $>$12\% of the oracle ceiling ($+29.90$\,pp) are the most promising direction (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}). Formal self-verification creates a \emph{symbolic mirage}---provably sound machinery adding no information beyond majority voting---and the path forward lies in structurally independent verification, guided by $K_\text{eff}$, BR, and $C_0$.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Three sequential Director instructions were received:
   
   **A. Figure 2 caption fix (completed):** Fix caption discrepancy — said "Twenty-seven" but figure shows 23 strategies.
   
   **B. α ablation integration MF3 (completed):** Integrate α ablation results into paper. Add one sentence in §5.2 main text + compact appendix table showing MAX-SAT vs count-only agreement across α∈{0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9} for Mistral-7B and Qwen2.5-14B FOLIO.
   
   **C. Discussion expansion (IN PROGRESS, page overflow unresolved):** Transform Discussion from 1-paragraph summary into 3-4 paragraph actionable section covering: (A) Practitioner Decision Framework using K_eff/BR/C₀, (B) SCB beyond SICA generalization, (C) Design Principles for escaping SCB, (D) Conclusion. Also compress §6 to make room, expand appendix extended discussion, maintain 8-page main text limit. Director explicitly stated: "编译后确认 8 页并报告."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - EMNLP 2026: 8-page strict main text limit, Limitations/References/Appendix unlimited
   - Symbolic Confirmation Bias (SCB): BR 1.66×-4.97× across nine models
   - α ablation: MAX-SAT vs count-only agreement ≥99% across all α values
   - Three diagnostics: K_eff (effective vote diversity), BR (bias ratio), C₀ (degenerate consensus)
   - Three escape conditions: structural independence, positive capability gap, task-verifier alignment
   - `\enlargethispage{N\baselineskip}` for page extension — currently at 8\baselineskip
   - Two-column ACL/EMNLP format with `\paragraph{}` sub-sections
   - Appendix section counter limit: 26 sections (A-Z), use `\paragraph` to avoid overflow

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - **discussion.tex** — The primary file being modified. Currently contains 3 \paragraph{} sections + merged conclusion.
     Current full content:
     ```latex
     \enlargethispage{8\baselineskip}
     \vspace{-4mm}
     \section{Discussion and Conclusion}
     \label{sec:discussion}
     \label{sec:conclusion}
     
     \paragraph{Practitioner decision framework.}
     \looseness=-1 Three zero-cost diagnostics predict self-verification failure before deployment. $K_\text{eff} \leq 1.3$: symbolic aggregation collapses to majority voting ($\Delta = -0.98$\,pp). SC $< 40\%$: constraints amplify errors ($\Delta = -2.83$\,pp). $C_0 < 5\%$: near-unanimous traces render aggregation moot. Only the intermediate regime (SC $\sim$50--60\%, $K_\text{eff} > 1.8$) offers marginal gain; practitioners should compute these before investing in symbolic reasoning.
     
     \paragraph{SCB beyond SICA.}
     \looseness=-1 SCB extends to any method extracting structured representations from a model's own outputs---self-verification \citep{huang2024selfcorrect}, self-refinement \citep{madaan2023selfrefine}, and chain-of-verification \citep{dhuliawala2023chainofverification} all face the same distributional prior. Our debate control ($\kappa = 0.15$, $-18.6$\,pp) confirms that independence and quality are at odds under same-model constraints.
     
     \paragraph{Design principles for escaping SCB.}
     \looseness=-1 The cross-architecture escape (\S\ref{sec:cross-arch}) identifies three necessary conditions: (i)~\emph{structural independence}---no shared architecture or training data; (ii)~\emph{positive capability gap}---the verifier's adjusted contribution exceeds the generator's SC; (iii)~\emph{task-verifier alignment}---the verification paradigm matches task structure. These explain why 27 same-model interventions fail ($\kappa \geq 0.40$) while a 406M encoder succeeds ($+11.00$\,pp). Trained extractors capturing $>$12\% of the oracle ceiling ($+29.90$\,pp) are the most promising direction (Appendix~\ref{app:extended-discussion}). Formal self-verification creates a \emph{symbolic mirage}---provably sound machinery adding no information beyond majority voting---and the path forward lies in structurally independent verification, guided by $K_\text{eff}$, BR, and $C_0$.
     ```
   
   - **solutions.tex** — §6 Cross-Architecture Proof-of-Concept, compressed to make room.
     Key changes:
     - "Why it works" compressed: removed (i)(ii)(iii) detailed descriptions, replaced with "structural independence, positive capability gap, and task-verifier alignment---expanded as design principles in \S\ref{sec:discussion}"
     - Removed `\enlargethispage{2\baselineskip}` before Capability gap
     - Capability gap: removed "four of six share the DeBERTa verifier---see Limitations" and "Process-κ gradient" sentence; appended "A $2{\times}2$ generator${\times}$extractor matrix confirms BR $> 1$ in all eight cells ($1.94$--$2.70$; Appendix~\ref{app:2x2})."
     - Entire "Regime-dependent bottleneck" paragraph REMOVED (was ~7 lines)
     - DRC compressed from 5 lines to: "DRC invokes NLI only below consensus threshold $\tau$, recovering 90\% of full-combo gain at ${\sim}$35\% NLI cost ($\tau{=}0.7$; Table~\ref{tab:drc}). Gains concentrate on weak generators (SC $< 40\%$), consistent with the capability gap. Regime-dependent bottleneck analysis appears in Appendix~\ref{app:2x2}."
   
   - **analysis.tex** — §5 Analysis
     - §5.2: Added α-insensitivity sentence after MAX-SAT vacuity: "This vacuity is $\alpha$-insensitive: agreement $\geq$99\% across $\alpha \in \{0.1, \ldots, 0.9\}$ for both high- and moderate-BR conditions (Table~\ref{tab:alpha-ablation})."
     - Figure 2 caption: Changed to "Twenty-three of 27 training-free strategies across four categories (four additional strategies tested but omitted for clarity)."
   
   - **appendix.tex**
     - Added α ablation table (tab:alpha-ablation) within "Constraint Ablation Details" section (after existing tab:ablation), showing agreement percentages for Mistral-7B (seed 42) and Qwen2.5-14B (seed 123) across α∈{0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9}
